- diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.

This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

text to make it sound more natural and human-written. Based on Wikipedia's
comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, negative
parallelisms, and excessive conjunctive phrases.

Use when the user says "review PR feedback", "go thru the PR comments", "address review comments", or similar.

None None
Nits and stale descriptions

**1. Trail description is pre-`--external`.** It still says "`entire agent list` now calls `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways()` before listing, so external agents appear in the output alongside built-in agents". The default path deliberately no longer discovers (commit d1b24dbe7). The PR body is current on this; the trail description is not.

**2. PR body Test section lists 2 tests, there are 5.** `TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath`, `_ExternalIsSuperset`, and `_EmptyStateWording` arrived in later commits.

**3. Unconditional footer (`agent_group.go:121-123`).** "Run 'entire agent list --external' to also list external plugins on your PATH." prints on every default invocation, including for the majority of users with nothing matching `entire-agent-*` on `$PATH`. Cheap discoverability against permanent noise on a command people run repeatedly — worth a conscious call either way.

**4. Unrelated drive-by (`agent/architecture_test.go`).** Moving `//nolint:staticcheck` onto the `parser.ParseDir` line is a correct fix — a `//nolint` directive does not apply when another comment line sits between it and the offending line — but it is unrelated to external-agent discovery and is not mentioned in the PR body.

**5. `mise run test:ci` not yet run**, per the PR body's own Verification section. Required before commit per CLAUDE.md. For what it is worth: `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) reports 0 issues on this head, and `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/...` plus the agent tests in `./cmd/entire/cli/` pass locally.

019ffaf8-3084-7ff5-bfa9-5b5dd661a8c7 low open 019ffa8c-c4e3-7855-9a24-4b4c38c6820c
None None
"Which agents are available" now has three implementations that can drift

`runAgentList`'s new loop (`agent_group.go:86-111`) inlines logic that already exists twice:

- the resolve-and-check-hooks body duplicates `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` (`config.go:86-98`) almost line for line
- the `agent.TestOnly` filter duplicates `StringList` (`registry.go:84-97`)

Both duplications are *justified* on their own terms — the new code needs the `Agent` value to call `external.IsExternal` and `AsHookSupport`, and neither helper returns it. But the result is that the test-only filter now has three separate answers in one command surface: `runAgentList` filters it, `StringList` filters it, and `printAgentError` does not (see the `vogon` finding). That is already a live inconsistency, not a hypothetical one.

Worth considering an `agent.ListResolved(ctx) []Agent` that resolves and applies the test-only filter once, which all three call sites could share. `dupl` does not trip at threshold 75 and `mise run lint` is clean, so this is a design note rather than a lint violation.
================================================================================
019ffaf8-1c33-7ea9-b86b-dfd6c1b0dfe9 low open 019ffa8c-c4e3-7855-9a24-4b4c38c6820c
None None
`SnapshotForTesting` doc overclaims concurrency safety, and it ships in the production binary

**Doc claim (registry.go:42-43):** "Both capture and restore hold registryMu, so it is safe against concurrent registry readers." True for readers. But restore does `registry = snapshot` — a wholesale replacement — so any `Register` that lands between capture and restore is silently discarded. It is not safe against concurrent *writers*, and the sentence reads as a general safety guarantee.

Benign today: every caller is a non-parallel test (they use `t.Setenv`/`t.Chdir`), Go does not run top-level parallel tests concurrently with serial ones, and `Register` almost always happens in `init`. Worth narrowing the sentence to what it guarantees, since the next caller will read it as blanket cover.

**Placement:** it lives in `registry.go`, so a testing-only helper is compiled into the shipped binary and exported to every importer of `agent`. It genuinely cannot go in `agent`'s `_test.go` — package `cli` needs it — but a dedicated `registry_testing.go`, or a small `agenttest` subpackage, would keep the intent legible at the call site. Noting the tradeoff was made rather than claiming it is wrong.

The helper itself is the right fix for a real problem, and the doc explains that problem well (temp-dir binaries leaking into the process-global registry so `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` execs deleted files). `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` covers it.
================================================================================
019ffaf7-e66a-7289-b8d5-f8c2fbbb85a1 low open 019ffa8c-c4e3-7855-9a24-4b4c38c6820c
None None
`--external` output does not distinguish external plugins from built-ins

Now that `--external` is a superset, the single flat list is the only output, and nothing marks which entries came from `$PATH`:

```
    opencode
    pi
    roger-roger    <- external plugin
    zed            <- external plugin
```

`roger-roger` and `zed` render identically to `claude-code`. That defeats the flag's purpose — a user passes `--external` precisely to see what discovery found on their PATH — and the distinction is trust-relevant, since external agents are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary.

A `(external)` suffix, or a second section under the built-ins, would make the superset legible. `external.IsExternal(ag)` is already computed one line above at `agent_group.go:98`, so the information is in hand.

This is a consequence of the superset change rather than a pre-existing gap: under the earlier "instead of" semantics the mode itself told you which list you were looking at.
================================================================================
019ffaf7-d20a-7360-8a57-9ffc0477e8ee medium open 019ffa8c-c4e3-7855-9a24-4b4c38c6820c
None None
`printWrongAgentError` is the one path in the agent group that stayed external-blind

Reproduced with `entire-agent-zed` on `$PATH`, using the branch binary:

```
$ entire agent add zedd
Unknown agent "zedd". Available agents:

  claude-code    (default)
  codex
  copilot-cli
  cursor
  factoryai-droid
  gemini
  opencode
  pi
  vogon

Usage: entire enable --agent <agent-name>
```

Three problems, in descending order of relevance to this PR:

**1. `zed` is absent.** Named discovery only resolves the name the user typed, so on the typo path nothing external is registered by the time `printAgentError` (`setup.go:1833-1846`) reads `agent.List()`. The user whose external plugin this PR just made addable gets an "Available agents" list that omits it — exactly the confusion #1928 was filed about, one keystroke away. The error path is the natural place to pay for a full scan, since it only runs when the command already failed: `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` before printing, or at minimum a line pointing at `entire agent list --external`.

**2. `vogon` (test-only) is listed.** `printAgentError` uses `agent.List()`, which does not filter `agent.TestOnly`; the new `runAgentList` does filter it (`agent_group.go:93-95`). Same command surface, two different answers to "what agents are available".

**3. Wrong usage line.** "Usage: entire enable --agent <agent-name>" when reached from `entire agent add`.

2 and 3 are pre-existing, but 2 is a direct inconsistency with the filtering this PR just added, and 3 gets more visible as `agent add` becomes the promoted path.
================================================================================
019ffaf7-9dd9-71d7-b84a-22a0448bed83 medium open 019ffa8c-c4e3-7855-9a24-4b4c38c6820c
None None
`--external` help text and variable name contradict the superset behavior

The final commit (30e08df9e, "make agent list --external a superset of the built-in listing") changed `--external` to list built-ins **and** external plugins, with `TestRunAgentList_ExternalIsSuperset` asserting it. Three artifacts still describe the old "instead of" semantics:

- `agent_group.go:70-71` flag help — "List external agent plugins found on your PATH **instead of** built-in agents"
- `agent_group.go:62` variable `externalOnly`, threaded through `runAgentList`'s signature — it is not "only"
- PR body — "`--external` lists external agent plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available)", omitting that built-ins come too

Verified against the built binary with `entire-agent-zed` on PATH:

```
$ entire agent list --external
Agents:
    claude-code
    ... (all 8 built-ins) ...
    roger-roger
    zed
```

The inline comment at `agent_group.go:96-97` has it right; only the user-facing text and the variable are stale. Suggest `includeExternal` and "Also list external agent plugins found on your PATH".

  Number:  992
  ID:      019fead0-928e-7562-b859-86751b5968f5

  Base:    main
  Status:  open

  Assignees: gtrrz-victor
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-10T08:36:04Z
  Updated: 2026-08-13T11:53:30Z

Description:
Problem:
The entire agent add, entire agent remove, and entire agent list commands did not discover external agent plugins (binaries on $PATH named entire-<agent-name>). Users could enable external agents with entire enable --agent <name>, but then couldn't manage them with the agent commands, breaking the expectation that agent management tools work consistently.
Solution:
Added external agent discovery to the agent management commands:
entire agent list now calls DiscoverAndRegisterAlways() before listing, so external agents appear in the output alongside built-in agents
entire agent add <name> now resolves the named external agent before registering it, executing only that specific binary rather than scanning all of $PATH
entire agent remove <name> similarly resolves the named external agent before removal
This makes agent discovery consistent across enable, add, remove, and list commands. The discovery bypasses the external_agents setting gate since these commands are themselves the explicit opt-in for agent management. Added a test to verify external agents appear in the listing.

`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.

Fixes #1928.

## Changes
- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)` before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`. A footer points at `--external`.
- **`--external`** lists external agent plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — same `Agents:` header, installed `✓` marker, and test-only filter — so output is uniform.
  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.

## Test
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagListsAvailablePlugin`: the default listing does not scan `$PATH` (an available external plugin is absent); `--external` lists it.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagMarksInstalled`: `--external` lists an installed external plugin marked `✓`.
- Both use an isolated repo and a `#!/bin/sh` mock plugin on `$PATH`; skip when no POSIX shell is available.

## Verification
- `mise run fmt` — clean
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) — 0 issues (cli + external pkgs)
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ -run 'AgentList|AgentGroup|ExternalAgent'` — PASS
- Benchmark (9 shell plugins on `$PATH`, `external_agents:true`): default `agent list` **18 execs → 0**; external listing moved behind `--external`. Full `mise run test:ci` not yet run.

- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`. A footer points at `--external`.

- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.
- **`printAgentError` (the "Unknown agent" / "Missing agent name" path) no longer contradicts `agent list`**:
  - It goes through the new `agent.ListResolved`, so test-only agents (`vogon`) are no longer advertised as available.
  - It does not scan `$PATH` (the error path should stay cheap), so it now points at `entire agent list --external` — otherwise the user whose external plugin this PR just made addable gets an "Available agents" list that omits it after a single typo.
  - The usage line follows the caller's command surface (`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` / `entire enable --agent`) instead of always printing `entire enable --agent`.

- Drive-by, unrelated to external agents: `agent/architecture_test.go` had `//nolint:staticcheck` separated from the `parser.ParseDir` call by another comment line, where the directive does not apply. Moved onto the offending line.

- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalIsSuperset`: `--external` includes both the external plugin and the built-ins.
- `TestRunAgentList_MarksExternalProvenance`: external lines carry `(external)`, built-in lines do not.
- `TestRunAgentList_EmptyStateWording`: mode-scoped empty state — "No built-in agents installed" by default, "No agents installed" under `--external`.
- `TestPrintAgentError_ExcludesTestOnlyAgents`, `TestPrintAgentError_PointsAtExternalListing`, and the usage-line assertion in `TestPrintWrongAgentError` cover the error-path fixes.
- `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` covers the registry snapshot helper.
- The external-plugin tests use an isolated repo and a `#!/bin/sh` mock plugin on `$PATH`; they skip when no POSIX shell is available.

- `mise run fmt` — clean
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) — 0 issues
- `mise run test:ci` — PASS
- Benchmark (9 shell plugins on `$PATH`, `external_agents:true`): default `agent list` **18 execs → 0**; external listing moved behind `--external`.

All 6 open findings addressed and resolved (14 resolved, 0 open). Committed as `0fb66015b` — **not pushed**, so you can review first.

**What changed**

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go` + new `registry_testing.go`:
- `ListResolved() []ResolvedAgent` — the single home for the test-only filter. `StringList` is now derived from it.
- `SnapshotForTesting` moved out of the production file; doc narrowed to what it actually guarantees (readers, not writers — restore replaces the whole map).

`cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go`:
- `externalOnly` → `includeExternal`; help text now "Also list external agent plugins found on your PATH".
- External entries get an `(external)` suffix.

`cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`:
- `printAgentError` filters test-only agents, points at `entire agent list --external` rather than scanning `$PATH` on an error path, and takes the caller's usage line.

Plus 3 new tests, an updated trail description, and a rewritten PR body.

**Two judgment calls I made, both reversible**

1. **Kept the unconditional footer** (finding #1 item 3). Discoverability for a new flag on a rarely-run command, and there's no way to know whether the user has plugins on `$PATH` without the very scan the default path exists to avoid.
2. **`ResolvedAgent` is a name+agent pair, not bare `[]Agent`.** Nothing in `discovery.go` validates an external plugin's self-reported `Name()` against the registry key derived from its binary, and the key is what users type and `agent.Get` accepts — so returning only the `Agent` would risk printing a name you can't then pass back in.

I also left `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` on the unfiltered list on purpose: e2e installs `vogon` hooks, so filtering test-only agents there would make `entire status` stop reporting them.

content.text:
That finding raised two separate points, and I handled them differently — one was a real fix, one was documentation only.

**Point 1 — the doc overclaimed.** The old sentence was:

> Both capture and restore hold registryMu, so it is safe against concurrent registry readers.

The finding's objection: that reads as a general safety guarantee, but restore does `registry = snapshot` — a wholesale map replacement — so any `Register` landing between capture and restore is silently discarded. I rewrote it to say exactly that, including who the callers are and why it's fine for them:

> Capture and restore both hold registryMu, so readers never observe a half-updated registry. Concurrent *writers* are not accounted for: restore replaces the whole map, so any Register that lands between capture and restore is discarded. Callers are serial tests, where that cannot happen.

**Point 2 — placement.** The finding noted a testing-only helper compiled into the shipped binary and exported to every importer of `agent`, and itself acknowledged it "genuinely cannot go in `agent`'s `_test.go`" because package `cli` needs it. It offered two options: a dedicated `registry_testing.go`, or an `agenttest` subpackage. I took the file split — new `cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry_testing.go` with a file-level comment explaining why it can't be a `_test.go`.

**What I did not do:** the helper is still in the production build. A `.go` file with `Testing` in the name is not a build-excluded file — only `_test.go` suffixes and build tags do that. So the split bought legibility at the call site, which is what the finding asked for ("would keep the intent legible"), but the binary contains the same code it did before. If you want it genuinely excluded, that needs the `agenttest` subpackage instead, or a build tag that the test harness sets — both larger changes that would touch every caller. Worth saying plainly since my resolve message could read as if the shipping concern went away.

The behavior is unchanged — no logic edits, just the move and the comment — and `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` still covers it.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push
- Always show the user what was committed and the PR URL when done

content.text:
No — I introduced a naming variant, not a repo pattern. Here's what the codebase actually does with cross-package test helpers:

**Dominant pattern: helper lives in the production file next to the code it manipulates, with a `ForTest`/`ForTesting` suffix as the "production must not call this" signal.** 6 helpers across 5 files:

| File | Helper |
|---|---|
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_command.go` | `SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting` — "Test-only." |
| `cmd/entire/cli/auth/cell_data_api.go` | `SetCellExchangeTransportForTest`, `SetResolveContextForCellAPIForTest` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/auth/data_api.go` | `SetResolveContextForAPIForTest` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/findings.go` | `PrintInvestigateFindingsListForTest` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/picker.go` | `SetPickerFormFnForTest` |

**Minority pattern: dedicated file** — only 2, and neither spelled the way I spelled it: `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/testing.go` (5 helpers, enough to justify its own file) and `redact/testhelpers.go` (whose header comment makes the same argument I made: *"Lives in a regular .go file (not export_test.go) so tests in cmd/entire/cli/strategy can call it. The 'ForTest' suffix is the production-code-must-not-call signal."*).

Two things this makes clear:

1. **The `agent` package already had its own precedent, and I broke it.** `SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting` sits inside `hook_command.go` — the production file whose behavior it overrides — which is exactly where `SnapshotForTesting` was in `registry.go` before I moved it. The pre-existing placement was already conventional for this package.
2. **`registry_testing.go` is a third filename spelling** that appears nowhere else. If a dedicated file were right, `testing.go` (matching `tokenstore`) would be the name.

And per the repo's own reasoning in `redact/testhelpers.go`, the `ForTesting` suffix *is* the signal — which `SnapshotForTesting` already carried before I touched it. So the move bought nothing the name wasn't already doing, and as I noted earlier it doesn't exclude the code from the shipped binary either.

I'd revert the move and keep the doc narrowing — that was the part with real substance. Which the finding also asked for, and which stands on its own.

1	package agent

3	import (
4		"maps"
5	
6		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
7	)
8	
9	// SnapshotForTesting captures the registry's current contents and returns a
10	// function that restores it to exactly that state.
11	//
12	// Tests that trigger agent registration as a side effect — external-agent
13	// discovery via runAgentList, for example — must defer or t.Cleanup the
14	// returned restore. Otherwise mock agents backed by t.TempDir binaries leak
15	// into the process-global registry and corrupt later tests in the package:
16	// GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled would exec their now-deleted binaries, and only
17	// TempDir cleanup ordering keeps that from mis-reporting installed agents.
18	//
19	// Capture and restore both hold registryMu, so readers never observe a
20	// half-updated registry. Concurrent *writers* are not accounted for: restore
21	// replaces the whole map, so any Register that lands between capture and
22	// restore is discarded. Callers are serial tests, where that cannot happen.
23	func SnapshotForTesting() func() {
24		registryMu.Lock()
25		defer registryMu.Unlock()
26		snapshot := make(map[types.AgentName]Factory, len(registry))
27		maps.Copy(snapshot, registry)
28		return func() {
29			registryMu.Lock()
30			defer registryMu.Unlock()
31			registry = snapshot
32		}
33	}

Comments earn their place by explaining non-obvious *current* behavior — load-bearing ordering, a gotcha, a deliberate tradeoff — not by tracking edits.

Absence checks are fine only when absence itself is the spec (e.g. "repo list has no filter section"). 1	## Summary
2	`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.
3	
4	Fixes #1928.
5	
6	## Changes
7	- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)` before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
8	- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`. A footer points at `--external`.
9	- **`--external`** is a **superset**: it lists the built-in agents *and* the external plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — same `Agents:` header, installed `✓` marker, and test-only filter — so output is uniform. External entries carry an `(external)` suffix, because they are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary, and that distinction is trust-relevant.
10	  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
11	- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.
12	- **`printAgentError` (the "Unknown agent" / "Missing agent name" path) no longer contradicts `agent list`**:
13	  - It goes through the new `agent.ListResolved`, so test-only agents (`vogon`) are no longer advertised as available.
14	  - It does not scan `$PATH` (the error path should stay cheap), so it now points at `entire agent list --external` — otherwise the user whose external plugin this PR just made addable gets an "Available agents" list that omits it after a single typo.
15	  - The usage line follows the caller's command surface (`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` / `entire enable --agent`) instead of always printing `entire enable --agent`.
16	- **New `agent.ListResolved() []ResolvedAgent`** is the single place the test-only filter lives; `StringList`, `runAgentList`, and `printAgentError` all go through it, so "which agents are available" has one answer across the command surface. It returns name+agent pairs because an external plugin's self-reported `Name()` is not validated against the registry key derived from its binary — and the registry key is the identity users type and `agent.Get` accepts. `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` deliberately stays on the unfiltered list: e2e installs `vogon` hooks and must keep seeing them.

36		defer registryMu.RUnlock()

48	// Use it to act on or report the state of what is actually registered:
49	// installing and uninstalling hooks, detecting which agent owns a transcript,
50	// listing agents whose hooks are installed. The Vogon canary must appear
51	// there — e2e installs its hooks, and omitting it would misreport the repo.
52	//
53	// Anything that offers the user a choice of agent wants ListAvailable or
54	// StringList instead; no picker, prompt, or "available agents" listing
55	// should advertise a test-only agent.
56	func List() []types.AgentName {
57		registryMu.RLock()
58		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
59	
60		names := make([]types.AgentName, 0, len(registry))
61		for name := range registry {
62			names = append(names, name)
63		}

66	}

70	// Get accepts; an external plugin's self-reported name can differ from the
71	// name derived from its binary, which is what it is registered under.
72	type ResolvedAgent struct {
73		Name  types.AgentName
74		Agent Agent
75	}
76

78	// order: every registered agent except the test-only ones. It is the single
79	// place the test-only filter is applied, so callers that need the Agent value
80	// (to check hook support or externality) get the same answer as callers that
81	// only need names via StringList.
82	//
83	// Agents that vanish from the registry between listing and resolving (a
84	// concurrent restore of a testing snapshot is the only way that happens) are
85	// skipped.

87		names := List()
88		agents := make([]ResolvedAgent, 0, len(names))

143	func AgentForTranscriptPath(transcriptPath, repoPath string) (Agent, bool) {
144		if transcriptPath == "" {

146		}

aiTitle: Review and fix PR trail findings

content.text:
You're right to push on it — and checking made me find I'd been asserting something false.

**What we decided, precisely:** always filter where we *offer or advertise a choice*. That part holds — all four such paths (`runAgentList`, `printAgentError`, `hookAgentOptions`, `StringList`) go through `ListAvailable`, and there are no inline `TestOnly` checks left.

**But my justification for why `List` must stay unfiltered was wrong.** I said repeatedly that `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` and `entire status` must see `vogon` because e2e installs its hooks. That's false — `vogon.AreHooksInstalled` returns `false` unconditionally (`agent/vogon/hooks.go:92`), and `InstallHooks` is a no-op, because the vogon binary fires hooks directly. So `vogon` never appears in that list at all. Filtering there would be a no-op, not a breakage.

**The real reason `List` must stay unfiltered** is `hooks_cmd.go:64`: it iterates `List()` to register the `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands, and `e2e/vogon/main.go:549` shells out to exactly `entire hooks vogon <verb>`. Filter there and the subcommand ceases to exist — every canary test breaks. Secondarily, `external/discovery.go` needs every taken name to avoid re-registering a colliding one. Both are non-display consumers, which is the honest distinction: not "display vs machinery," but **user-facing choice vs the registry's own plumbing**.

**And there's still one leak I hadn't looked at** — `Get()`'s own error string, `registry.go:40`:

```go
return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
```

That's a user-facing "available:" listing that advertises `vogon`, same bug class as the finding. `printWrongAgentError` intercepts the common paths, but wherever a command returns this error straight through, `main.go` prints it verbatim.

The fix isn't a one-liner, which is why I want your call rather than just doing it: `Get` formats that message while holding `registryMu.RLock()`, and `StringList` → `ListAvailable` → `Get`/`List` would re-enter the read lock (and call factories) underneath it. content.text:
**To answer your question directly:** yes — we agreed to always filter, and I'd left one place unfiltered. `List` vs `StringList` differ in return type *and* filtering, and that second difference is invisible in the names, which is how `Get`'s error string kept advertising `vogon` right after I claimed the filter had one home.

What I got wrong earlier and should correct plainly: I justified `List` staying unfiltered by saying `entire status` must show `vogon` because e2e installs its hooks. That's false — `vogon.AreHooksInstalled` returns `false` unconditionally and `InstallHooks` is a no-op, so `vogon` never appears there. The genuine reason `List` must stay unfiltered is `hooks_cmd.go`: it registers `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` from `List()`, and the vogon binary shells out to `entire hooks vogon <verb>` — filter it and every canary test breaks. That's plumbing, not display.

The `Get` fix is in, with the lock released before formatting the error so `StringList` can't re-enter `registryMu`. I confirmed the test goes red without the fix (it printed `vogon`-style probe in the available list) and green with it, and `go test -race` on the package passes since I touched locking.

That wrong justification is also published — it's in the `78cbf717e` commit message and the PR body. I'll fix the PR body when the suite finishes; the commit message is immutable without a rewrite, which I won't do on a pushed branch unless you ask.
